grammar.title: Grammar
grammar.rule: わたしは、えほんがすきです。すきなほんをよみます。

The な form immediately modifies the following noun — translated in the note

tables.caption: Preference が versus the direct object を — translated in the note

grammar.note_en:
すき and きらい describe a preference; they are not action verbs. わたしはえほんがすきです means “I like picture books.” は marks the person as topic, and が marks the thing liked in this preference frame. わたしはうたがきらいです means “I dislike songs.” Do not make a verb ending such as すきます. Ren and Yui describe their own preferences, not universal rules about adults or children.

Yui dislikes the newspaper and Ren likes it; the same material can receive different preferences. Haru likes her song but has difficulty making out the small handwriting. A preference does not by itself state reading ability. This chapter uses affirmative preference descriptions only. Adjective negatives and adjective/noun past forms are deferred to their later chapters.

すき and きらい belong to the na-adjective group. Before a noun use な: すきなほん is “a book one likes”; きらいなほん is “a book one dislikes”; すきなうた is “a song one likes.” The person is supplied by the surrounding topic or possessor. In this chapter’s scene, Yui’s すきなほん is her preferred book. This is ordinary adjective+noun modification, not a new plain relative clause. Before です, do not add な. A preference modifier can retain its liked thing: しんぶんがすきなひと means “a person who likes newspapers.” The predicate remains a na-adjective, not a new plain verb relative clause.

The final comparison table translates えほんがすきです as “I like picture books,” and しんぶんをよみます as “I read the newspaper.” を still marks the direct object of a reading action. が in the liking pattern does not become a general replacement for を. The already known existence use of が, as in ここにほんがあります, “There is a book here,” is a different construction.

じゅんばん is the order of turns. The bounded adverbial expression じゅんばんに means “in turns/in order”; the volunteers’ concrete four turns are Yui/picture book, Ren/newspaper, Mei/story and Haru/song. They use different materials in successive turns instead of requiring one volunteer to perform a disliked choice. The programme draft is written on the reverse of a shop price memo. It is distinct from the four new public invitation copies and from the two earlier staff cards.

The basic understanding frame marks the understood thing with が: じゅんばんがわかります means “I understand the order of turns.” めいさんのちいさいもじがわかりません means “I cannot make out Mei’s small characters” in this specific handwriting context. The familiar topic/contrast particle は can replace が: じゅんばんはわかります means “As for the order, I understand it,” contrasting it with the unclear handwriting. わかりません is its taught polite nonpast negative; it is not a potential conjugation of よみます. Haru reads the normal large print on the song sheet/book. Her difficulty concerns Mei’s small fresh handwritten title, not literacy in general or an inability to recognise old sign painting.

えほん means picture book; keep the complete compound intact. え is a picture, and もじ is a written character or lettering here. Learn えほん as a complete word; practise え separately when it means a picture. A しんぶん is a newspaper, and ものがたり is a story. こえ is voice; おおきいこえ and ちいさいこえ in the story mean a loud and a soft voice. うた is a song; うたいます means sing. No audio asset is needed to resolve those meanings: the delivered English meanings and the actual role trials supply support.

The script stage writes familiar sheet counts, price units and old/new descriptions. Keep their complete taught readings: the same numeral does not predict every person-counter or price reading. The new genre words and practice remain kana, and story kanji keep visible authored readings.

notes: Original contemporary Japanese narrative, public notices, book/song labels, exercises and vector scenes. No authentic quotation, adapted text, private archived letter or unopened parcel content is used. No audio asset is generated or assumed as meaning support.

Four connected stages preserve the full 40 workbook +8 A +8 B +6 C responses. Preference changes the reading plan; actual trials lead to four successive voices/materials, followed by a specific fresh-handwriting obstacle.

The formal town reading remains tomorrow evening/day6, separate from the already-held13th small meeting and the later historical map exhibition. Four new named volunteer invitation copies are not an attendee cap; older staff cards stay separate. No new spending, cupboard diagnosis, bundle contents or map author is invented.

Five open slots stay within the22-unit ceiling: stable ja-22-07 えらびます and ja-17-05 じゅんばん move earlier; sing, bounded understanding and programme are new scene needs. Future allocated IDs are not duplicated.

The actual eight new characters are 一四枚百千円古新, supporting already-known whole sheet-count/price/adjective surfaces. New genre/liking words remain kana, including the intact compound えほん. No substring substitution turns it into an artificial mixed spelling or turns います into a time word. Every story Han has authored exact-source readings.
The in-memory candidate retains part2’s 88% prior-atom floor. Any lower measured coverage remains a visible advisory for independent judgment; no threshold is changed or numerical padding added.

Haru is an adult retired sign painter who reads normal large print and her song sheet. Mei’s small fresh handwritten song-title field is the specific difficulty; the understood turn order and Haru’s broader lettering knowledge remain intact.

The shop memo’s financial face and programme reverse remain distinct. The paid blue parts box and Haru’s red tool case stay closed; the four public copies are separate from the one cramped programme draft.
